label: Rosa (carer → coordinator)
tagline: Two decades of care: aide, nurse, coordinator, and the Sunday table that held a whole family together.

entries.title: Care aide, first ward
entries.body: Started as a hospital care aide. Night shifts, strong coffee, kind nurses. Family said I was born for this; my feet disagreed.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2006
entries.body: Year 2006: the Sunday table held. Work hard, family harder, rest scheduled like medicine.

entries.title: Sunday lunches begin
entries.body: Started Sunday lunches at Mama Elena’s: twelve people, one table, no phones. The family operating system.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2007
entries.body: Year 2007: a caring year in every direction. Roster updated, hearts too.

entries.title: Back and lifting
entries.body: Lifting patients wrecked my back at 24. Physio, technique, asking for help — a skill I resisted for years.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2008
entries.body: Year 2008: pivots and night shifts, but lunch was at one and nobody missed it.

entries.title: Medication systems
entries.body: Learned medication scheduling systems cold. Colour codes, double checks, calm under alarms.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2009
entries.body: Year 2009: I learned to accept care as well as give it. Growth, Rosa-style.

entries.title: Papa Miguel diagnosed
entries.body: Dad’s heart diagnosis. I became the family scheduler overnight. Care is logistics plus love.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2010
entries.body: Year 2010: the Sunday table held. Work hard, family harder, rest scheduled like medicine.

entries.title: Care costs spreadsheet
entries.body: Built the family care-cost spreadsheet everyone pretends not to need. Funerals, meds, transport: priced with love.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2011
entries.body: Year 2011: a caring year in every direction. Roster updated, hearts too.

entries.title: Pivot: train properly
entries.body: Decided to train as a nurse properly, nights and weekends. The ward taught me first; school will credential it.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2012
entries.body: Year 2012: pivots and night shifts, but lunch was at one and nobody missed it.

entries.title: Fatima, study sister
entries.body: Fatima and I studied through every night class. She quizzed me on the bus; I kept her awake with empanadas.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2013
entries.body: Year 2013: I learned to accept care as well as give it. Growth, Rosa-style.

entries.title: Burnout, recognised
entries.body: I cared for everyone except me. Burnout leave, six weeks. Mama Elena moved in and cared for the carer.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2014
entries.body: Year 2014: the Sunday table held. Work hard, family harder, rest scheduled like medicine.

entries.title: Qualified nurse
entries.body: Qualified at last, oldest in my cohort, proudest too. The pivot took five years of nights. Worth every one.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2015
entries.body: Year 2015: a caring year in every direction. Roster updated, hearts too.

entries.title: Discharge fails families
entries.body: Finding: discharges fail at the kitchen table, not the hospital. Families need one page, not forty.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2016
entries.body: Year 2016: pivots and night shifts, but lunch was at one and nobody missed it.

entries.title: One-page care plans
entries.body: Method: one-page care plans families actually use: meds, meals, red flags, who to call. Adopted ward-wide.

entries.title: Papa Miguel, goodbye
entries.body: Dad died at home, us around him, Sunday lunch still warm. Grief is a roster change nobody wants.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2017
entries.body: Year 2017: I learned to accept care as well as give it. Growth, Rosa-style.

entries.title: Mama Elena moves in
entries.body: Mum moved in after Dad. Three generations, one bathroom, much laughter. Care became home-shaped.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2018
entries.body: Year 2018: the Sunday table held. Work hard, family harder, rest scheduled like medicine.

entries.title: Community care models
entries.body: Researched community care cooperatives. Families like mine are infrastructure; policy just hasn’t noticed.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2019
entries.body: Year 2019: a caring year in every direction. Roster updated, hearts too.

entries.title: Pandemic ward
entries.body: COVID ward spring. Video calls held families together through glass. I coordinated and cried in stairwells.

entries.title: My own scare
entries.body: Brief hospital stay, exhaustion and infection. The cared-for carer again. Family roster activated without me asking.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2020
entries.body: Year 2020: pivots and night shifts, but lunch was at one and nobody missed it.

entries.title: Pivot: coordination
entries.body: Moving from bedside to care coordination: fewer shifts, wider reach. My Sunday-table skills, professionalised.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2021
entries.body: Year 2021: I learned to accept care as well as give it. Growth, Rosa-style.

entries.title: Family roster method
entries.body: Method: the family roster — named humans, named jobs, rest built in. Shared with every family I coordinate.

entries.title: Mum’s care fund
entries.body: Siblings pooled a care fund for Mum, transparent spreadsheet, no drama. Past-Rosa’s spreadsheet obsession vindicated.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2022
entries.body: Year 2022: the Sunday table held. Work hard, family harder, rest scheduled like medicine.

entries.title: Co-op pilot
entries.body: Piloting a carers cooperative in our district: twenty families, shared respite, shared knowledge.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2023
entries.body: Year 2023: a caring year in every direction. Roster updated, hearts too.

entries.title: Lucia qualifies
entries.body: Niece Lucia qualified as a nurse. I pinned her badge. The family care line continues, chosen this time.

entries.title: Respite is medicine
entries.body: Finding across 40 families: scheduled respite prevents crisis admissions better than any leaflet. Rest is treatment.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2024
entries.body: Year 2024: pivots and night shifts, but lunch was at one and nobody missed it.

entries.title: Mama Elena at 90
entries.body: Mum turned 90 at the Sunday table, 22 of us, she beat everyone at dominoes. Care returned as celebration.

entries.title: Teaching coordination
entries.body: Teaching care coordination to new nurses: logistics as love language, rosters as kindness.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2025
entries.body: Year 2025: I learned to accept care as well as give it. Growth, Rosa-style.

entries.title: It all threads
entries.body: Aide, daughter-carer, nurse, coordinator. Every pivot was care changing shape. Twenty years, one table, it works out.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2026
entries.body: Year 2026: the Sunday table held. Work hard, family harder, rest scheduled like medicine.
